$comment: Hard limits enforced by tools/vitest/budgetReporter.mjs on every run. Per-file and per-test limits sit at about twice the current worst case; suite totals may exceed the baseline by the tolerance. Totals are per-file sums (not wall clock) but still swing ~1.5x with machine load, so the gate is tuned to catch a doubling, not drift. Refresh the baseline here, in the same change, when the suite legitimately grows.
$comment_maxTestMs: Must stay above src/test/setup.ts's asyncUtilTimeout (15s), or a test that spends the DOM ceiling waiting for something that never arrives is reported here as a budget violation instead of as the failure it is. The slowest healthy test is ~5s, so 20s still catches a doubling.
$comment_baseline: Refreshed 2026-09-03 with the conversation UI (plan P2). The 105-file figure it replaced was already stale — the suite held 123 files before this phase, which added one. importMs grew because every page test that reaches a conversation now loads a real markdown renderer (streamdown, ~260ms) where the hand-written block parser it replaced cost nothing; measured 147-240s across runs. testMs is raised for a different reason: it is a per-file sum, so it inflates with worker contention rather than with this change — AgentGroupsPage.test.tsx is 8s alone against 39s under full fan-out — and the previous 120s no longer described what the suite measures. Mermaid, LaTeX and streamdown's own code plugin were dropped rather than budgeted for; mermaid alone was ~950ms per importing file.
